main_text.p: mia dñna & præsidia cuiquam uestrûm cõ ferri,persuasum habeam:eaq; non uobis so lum, sed generis humani societati, ex toto corde meo gratuler.

Verumenimuero, ut ad uos ueniam, si magna est eorû Germania nostra Rerum-pub. & Principum laus, qui initio renascentis Euangelij,non sine magno suo labo-re & periculo aperuerunt portas Iehoua exercituum, ac non ipsi solùm sunt amplexi incorruptam & salutarẽ Euangelij doctrinam, sed etiam subditos suos ad eiusdẽ studium inuitârunt: magna sanè laus est etiam laudatissimorum uestrorum Maio-rum,quos omnium primos, abiecta Ponti-ficiorum τὴν ἑτεροδοξαν καὶ ματαιο-λογίαν & tetra idolomania, Euangelion Christi amplexos fuisse, ac ueritatis uexil-lum in fortissima Polonorum gente (quæ professo populos Scythicos longo iam tem-pore repressit, & nunc uictricib.armis im-manè Moscorum rabiem contundit)erexis-se: ac uirtute in fide, ueramq; perseueran-tiam & constantiâ in religiosissimo hoc in-stituto,haftenus probatisse,uidemus. Det Dominus

page.notes: Abbreviations and the Greek phrase τὴν ἑτεροδοξαν καὶ ματαιολογίαν were read from a small scan; the Greek is the most doubtful part and may contain errors. "haftenus" in the scan reads as "hactenus" in the printed text, so it is marked as likely; the last words are doubtful. Line "uictricib.armis" has a stop before "armis" as printed. The last line "Dominus" is the catchword-like line at the foot but is part of the text, so it is kept in main text.
